summary:
M.A.R.S: Mission Ares Risk Simulator is a 2D interactive mars outpost simulator designed to train junior astronauts in habitat survival, enviromental management and emergency decision making.
We developed a dynamic simulation based in real NASA life-support engineering (ECLSS), radiation shielding protocols, and Martian surface hazards. Players manage critical habitat modules—such as life support systems, panoramic observation, geophysics experiments and airlock security measures—while responding to problems like the system failure of pressure drops, CO2 buildup, analysis of martian soil dust and checking the astronaut suits. The project directly addresses the challenge of translating complex space-habitat engineering into an accessible, easy hands-on learning experience. By turning abstract aerospace constraints into risk management scenarios. It is important because preparing the next generation of explorers requires work, dedication and available real information about missions on mars. We have included an encyclopedia with brief information about the missions that were carried out, including the coordinates of the Jezero Crater and how the system works.
details: M.A.R.S. bridges the gap between complex aerospace engineering documentation and accessible STEM education. By translating authentic NASA technical standards into easy gameplay mechanics. The simulator strengthens systems thinking, scientific data and crisis-management skills among young learners. Its intended impact is to inspire the next generation of space explorers and engineers by demonstrating how physics, chemistry, and human-factors engineering work together to sustain human life in a simpler way. We used Pygame (Python Game) for the code and also, the style is 2D because of the simplicity and esthetic retro vibe that we'd like to give to the young generations since we considered that it would attract more public if it had some ''undertale'' esthetic combinated with space and science.
